claims.paraphrase: On 17 December 1987 the Belka Federation undergoes legal reforms; Belkan military expenditures increase, political power is transferred to countries in the east, and troops stationed there are withdrawn to Belka proper.
claims.disposition: implemented by inherited mod content (mod provenance owner); official date is a reference anchor
claims.conflicts: The mod names the reforms the 'Belkan Federal Law Review'; the official text says only 'legal reforms'. The mod dates that Review to 1987 (belka_dlp_coup.5.d, ac_news_event.3.d) and to 1988 (osea_glrdc.2.d, osea.77.d, UST_start_desc, UST_GATHERING_STORM_DESC, GEB_GATHERING_STORM_DESC, ustio.1.d, ustio.2.d), an internal inconsistency; officially the reforms are 1987 / 12.17 and the two independences are 1988. osea_glrdc.2.d adds Osean secret support for the independence movements, which the source does not state. Country name 'Belkan Federation' versus official 'The Belka Federation'. No ledger row cites this date.
claims.unknowns: What the legal reforms contained, which 'countries in the east' received political power, what powers were transferred, how many troops were withdrawn, and whether the reforms and the 1988 independences are the same act (the source does not link them). The mod's 'Federal Law Review' name and the Osean-support motive are not in the source.

claims.paraphrase: On 8 October 1990 construction begins on facilities to protect the Excalibur base; Osea declares rearmament; and Estovakia abandons its northeastern offshore oil facilities.
claims.disposition: implemented by inherited mod content (mod provenance owner); official date is a reference anchor
claims.conflicts: Partial coverage only: only the Osea rearmament clause appears in inherited mod content (osea.20.d backstory, mod provenance owner); the Excalibur protective construction and the Estovakian abandonment are not covered; the official date is a reference anchor. (1) Osea rearmament: inherited osea.20.d attaches the 'Rearmament Declaration' to President Daniel Andrews at the start of his presidency; the source names no person, office or content, and Andrews is mod provenance. (2) Excalibur protection: nothing is dated to 1990; the mod's defensive installations (RTLS systems, 'Excalibur Secured', the hardening programme) are mod provenance or provisional gameplay tied to the war or to 1994 / 12.23. (3) Estovakia: the abandonment is not scripted or cited; docs/ANEA_FOUNDATION.md:60 only disclaims a restored facility. The 2008 / 07.15 entry (oil platforms in the northeast held by a public corporation, taken and restored by the Eastern Faction) is not linked to this entry by the source, so whether they are the same facilities, and whether the Wave B text EVA_ecw_oil_register_desc conflicts with this entry, is unknown. This entry bundles three statements about three countries under one citation.
claims.unknowns: What protective facilities were built, by whom, and whether they were finished; what Osea's rearmament comprised, who declared it and why; why Estovakia abandoned the facilities, how many there were, who owned them in 1990, and whether they are the same as the northeastern oil platforms the 2008 / 07.15 entry says were held by a public corporation (the source does not link the two entries). No causal link between the three statements is given.

claims.conflicts: (1) Recipients: the inherited belka.9 transfers states to Osea, Ustio, FATO, Gebet and Sapin; the official sentence names FATO, unnamed 'neighboring eastern nations' and the Osean Federation, and never names Ustio, Gebet or Sapin as recipients. (2) Terms: officially the northern territory is sold cheaply to FATO and the northern islands and Great Lakes region are ceded (not sold) to Osea; the mod presents one Osean-brokered deal in which 'the Oseans will pay us a rather high sum of money' and Belka is 'selling a portion of the Great Lakes to Osea itself' (belka.8.d). (3) Timing: the mod's sale is undated and focus-driven after the liberal election win (belka.7 -> osea_glrdc.1/.2 -> belka.8 -> BLK_sell_the_land -> belka.9); officially the sales (08.29) follow the discovery of the Great Lakes Resource Development Company's concealed losses (08.16), whereas the mod forms the company after the sale. (4) The mod bundles the state transfers (a border redraw) into the sale event, while the Chronicle gives a separate 'borders are redrawn' entry on 12.16. (5) belka.9 also dispatches recta.1 ('The Question of Recta') to Gebet after 90 days and ustio.1 ('Offer from Ratio'), ustio.3 and ustio.4 to Ustio; the Ustio-to-Ratio cession news ac_news_event.2 is fired later by a Ustio focus (common/national_focus/UST_shared.txt:235), not by belka.9. (7) The ledger row cites the date but scripts nothing from it; the only implementation of a sale is the inherited, unsourced chain.
claims.unknowns: Which 'neighboring eastern nations' bought the eastern territory; which 'northern islands' were ceded; what 'cheaply' means; whether the three transactions were one treaty or separate; the state/province extent of each transfer (not to be mapped); who negotiated and why. claims.conflicts: (1) The official-sourced content (ac_sp_excalibur, 'Excalibur Hardening Programme') only strengthens a tower that the inherited, undated focus BLK_excalibur builds inside the DLP branch; so in play Excalibur may be completed before or after 23 December 1994 or never, and the Chronicle completion date is not enforced (the ledger states this). (2) The inherited belka_dlp_coup.6 and the 'uses Excalibur for hostile nations' event give Excalibur a chosen role (anti-aircraft, anti-land, anti-ICBM) and a destruction meter; the chunk says nothing about what Excalibur is or does. (3) The project and fallback-decision text (ac_sp_excalibur_desc, ac_superweapons_excalibur_desc) goes beyond this chunk: 'the engineers declared it complete' embellishes 'Belka completes Excalibur'; the 1981 ballistic-missile-defence programme origin is supported by the official Super Weapons page (Excalibur), but 'chemical laser' is not (that page says only 'laser superweapon'), and 'stands above the Belkan lowlands' contradicts that page ('constructed in the hilly southern region of Tauberg, within the Principality of Belka'). claims.unknowns: What Excalibur is, where it stands, which Belkan body or contractor built it and when construction began, what 'completes' means operationally (tested, commissioned, or structurally finished), and its purpose; none of these are stated in the 12.23 sentence.

claims.paraphrase: The President of the FCU announces globally that Ulysses will impact Earth and announces plans to counter it. Richard Payne, head of the FCU Department of Defense, orders all personnel under FCU command to temporarily return home. FCU Secretary of State Stateson explains to UTO headquarters how a National Missile Defense (NMD) system could be used to protect against the asteroid's impact and seeks the understanding of the allied nations. An assassination attempt is made on the President of Osea.
claims.conflicts: Only the first two sentences (the announcement and counter-plans) are covered. (a) Mod text (ac_pwi.70.d, ac_sp_stonehenge_desc) attributes the announcement to 'the FCU'; the Chronicle attributes it to 'the President of the FCU', whom it does not name. The user-approved provisional FCU leader at the 1991 start is Robert Sinclair (docs/CANON_LEDGER.md:55); the ledger does not place him in office in 1996, so no text should say Sinclair made the announcement. (b) Richard Payne's recall order, Stateson's NMD explanation to UTO headquarters, and the assassination attempt on the President of Osea have no ledger row, script or localisation; UTO exists only as inherited idea names. (c) The mod's Osean president in 1996 is an inherited election result (Daniel Andrews / Tyler Mackenzie, mod provenance), while the official sentence names nobody; an attempt must not be scripted against a named mod leader. (d) ac_sp_stonehenge opens on this date as a provisional gate (labelled). (e) Grep for 'Payne', 'Stateson', 'Riass', 'Missile Defense', 'NMD' returns no hits.
claims.unknowns: The FCU President's name; the content of the counter-plans; how long the personnel recall lasted; whether UTO or the allied nations accepted the NMD explanation and which nations they were; who made the assassination attempt, where, and whether it failed (the sentence says only 'attempt'); the Osean President's name; whether the four statements are related to one another beyond sharing the date.

claims.paraphrase: The FCU completes Stonehenge in a desert region of the neutral country San Salvacion. Former top pilots from the Belkan Air Force are hired by various countries and work as aggressor squadrons. The Erusean Air and Space Administration begins development of the X-02.
people: former top pilots from the Belkan Air Force (unnamed group)
places: a desert region of San Salvacion (unnamed)
units_ships_squadrons: aggressor squadrons (former Belkan Air Force pilots, text only)
claims.conflicts: (a) Stonehenge in the mod is an FCU special project that may finish on any date after 20 April 1996 or never; 19 June 1998 is a target, not enforced (labelled). (b) The mod's Stonehenge location, state 310 'San Salvacion', is labelled provisional; the Chronicle names only a desert region. (c) The inherited history starts SNS inside the FCU faction, while the Chronicle calls San Salvacion neutral (recorded difference, USEAN_CONTINENTAL_WAR.md:82). (d) ac_pwi.75 says the pilots serve 'abroad as aggressor instructors'; the source says they are 'hired by various countries and work as aggressor squadrons' — 'instructors' is not in the source. (e) ac_pwi.75 fires only on the Belkan defeat path; the source attaches no outcome condition. (f) The mod's Stonehenge text adds 'eight railguns' and 'FCU-led international project' from the Super Weapons page, which this chunk does not include. (g) The X-02 sentence and the Erusean Air and Space Administration are covered nowhere.
claims.unknowns: What Stonehenge is and what it is for (this entry does not say; 'eight railguns' and its purpose come from the Super Weapons page, not this chunk); when its construction began; which countries hired the pilots and which pilots; what the X-02 is (no aircraft type or role is given) and when its development ended; the exact site inside San Salvacion; whether anyone besides the FCU built Stonehenge (this entry credits the FCU alone); whether the three statements share more than the date.

The fragments fell for weeks ... towns that no longer appear on the maps, roads cut by craters'), ac_sp_arkbird_desc ('low orbit became a hazard: debris crowded the paths of satellites'), YUK_arkbird_debris_talks_desc ('The fragments of Ulysses are still falling'). None of these consequences is in this entry; some may rest on the Super Weapons pages (Stonehenge, Megalith, Arkbird), which this chunk does not include. Every ledger uses 8 July 1999 as the crisis handoff while stating it is not an impact timestamp; the Usean partner and Anea focus trees cut civil preparation off on this date as a gameplay rule.
claims.unknowns: What followed the Roche-limit passage (break-up, impacts, where, casualties): this sentence states none of it; the time of day; which fragments fell where; the Chronicle's later entries, not in this chunk, are the only official basis for consequences.

claims.conflicts: (a) ac_sp_arkbird opens on 8 July 1999 (Roche limit), so Osea can start or even complete the conversion before 8 October 1999 and without Yuktobania; the cooperation is optional via ac_yuk_arkbird_partner and the Yuktobanian branch opens on 8 October 1999. The ledger labels the gate provisional. (b) Mod text says 'Osea proposes converting its Arkbird aircraft ... and invites Yuktobanian engineers' and 'Osea's answer is the Arkbird, the great aircraft built to fly at the edge of space'; the Chronicle sentence says only that the two countries cooperate and does not say who proposed it, who owns the Arkbird, or what it is. (c) ac_cpw.14 calls the Arkbird 'completed under the joint Osean–Yuktobanian programme', a completion this entry does not state (it cites the Super Weapons page, not in this chunk). (d) YUK text 'The fragments of Ulysses are still falling' is not in this entry.
claims.unknowns: Who proposed the cooperation; what the Arkbird was before conversion, who built it and where; where the conversion took place; when it finished; the terms of the cooperation; whether other countries took part.

claims.paraphrase: On 10 January 2000 Emmeria enacts an aid program to help Estovakia recover from Ulysses. The assistance is later frozen because of delayed infrastructure repairs, chronic material shortages, and conflicts and looting by certain military factions.
claims.conflicts: The Continental War ledger (docs/USEAN_CONTINENTAL_WAR.md) still lists 2000 / 01.10 as reference-only for its round, while docs/ANEA_CAMPAIGNS.md and docs/ANEA_EXPANSION_LEDGER.md record it as implemented in the Anea campaign; the two ledgers describe different rounds, not a factual contradiction. The mod's freeze is a provisional service-stage mechanic (monitored versus failed distribution), and 'looting by certain military factions' is not represented by any named faction.
claims.unknowns: The source gives no freeze date, no aid amounts, no duration, and does not name the military factions involved in the conflicts and looting.

claims.paraphrase: In the summer (the chunk places this text inside the 2002 / 03.20 entry; the day and month are not given) Erusea invades the neutral country of San Salvacion, seizes Stonehenge and begins using its railguns as anti-air batteries.

The mod's Stonehenge location (state 310) is provisional; the source gives no state. The mod's ac_ucw.20 text calls Stonehenge 'the eight-gun railgun battery', a detail not in this entry.
claims.unknowns: The source gives only a season, no day or month; it does not say how the invasion was conducted, how long the seizure took, whether San Salvacion resisted, or which aircraft the railguns were used against.

During the Lighthouse War, Osean forces seized the one remaining railgun battery, which was disabled when struck by a fragment of Ulysses, and used it as a trump card in their offense.
